children: In the third quarter, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials) reported a $1.1 billion noncash charge that was mostly related to stock warrants issued under its supply agreements for artificial intelligence chips with OpenAI and Meta.
Although the charge had an impact on reported earnings, the company's cash flow was unaffected.
According to Chief Financial Officer Jean Hu, the cost represented shifts in AMD's stock price as well as the projected likelihood that clients will fulfill the terms of the warrants.
Including the penalty, AMD reported earnings of $1.46 per share using generally accepted accounting standards.
As it dispatched MI450-series graphics processing units in accordance with client agreements, the company started to recognize the accounting impact.
The warrants enable OpenAI and Meta to acquire sizeable stock shares, provided that performance and other contractual objectives are met.

The arrangements strengthen AMD's commercial ties with major AI customers but introduce potential dilution for existing shareholders. They also highlight how AI suppliers are using equity incentives to secure long-term demand.

title: AMD's OpenAI and Meta Deals Come With a $1 Billion Catch
